mainTopic: The Shabbat changeover of the משמרות: why the incoming משמר gets two extra loaves of לחם הפנים, the refutation of רב יהודה's claim that the מוספין are also divided, and why each group divides its bread in the north or the south.
overview: On the שבת when the weekly priestly shifts (משמרות) change, the two groups divide the לחם הפנים. According to רבי יהודה in the משנה, the incoming group takes seven loaves and the outgoing group five. רבי יצחק explains that the two extra loaves are payment for locking the Temple doors. אביי explains why the groups don't simply cancel the extra: a sure gain now is better than a possible gain later. רב יהודה then adds that the מוספין are also divided, but he is refuted by a ברייתא of דבי שמואל, which discusses dividing portions and mentions only the bread. The גמרא next explains that the incoming group divides in the north and the outgoing group in the south, so everyone can see who is coming and who is going. The משמר of בילגה always divides in the south as a penalty. It was punished either because מרים בת בילגה insulted the מזבח or because the משמר came late. אביי explains the group penalty with the rule 'woe to the wicked, woe to his neighbor,' and מסכת סוכה ends on the hopeful note 'good for the righteous, good for his neighbor.'

steps.title: What are the two extra loaves for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the incoming משמר receives two more loaves of לחם הפנים than the outgoing משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these two extra loaves — what is their purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the משנה: why does the incoming group get two extra loaves? This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are twelve loaves of לחם הפנים. The תנא קמא of the משנה splits them evenly, six and six, but רבי יהודה in the משנה says the incoming group takes seven and the outgoing group five. The גמרא wants to know what justifies, according to רבי יהודה, giving the incoming group two more loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their purpose / what are they for?
The showbread, the twelve loaves placed on the שולחן each שבת

phrases.english: And these two (extra loaves)
phrases.notes: Refers to the gap between the seven loaves and the five loaves in רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.

phrases.english: what is their purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens analysis of רבי יהודה's uneven 7/5 split in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the incoming משמר gets two extra loaves.

steps.title: Payment for locking the doors
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that the two extra loaves are payment for the incoming group's job of closing the Temple doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: They are payment for locking the doors.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question: the incoming group gets two extra loaves as a fee for locking the Temple doors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The incoming group takes on the work of closing up the מקדש, so it is paid for that extra job. The extra loaves are therefore not favoritism. They are wages for a specific task.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
As payment for locking the doors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two extra loaves are wages for locking the Temple doors.

steps.title: Why not just cancel it out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the outgoing group doesn't say: let each of us give up the extra, since it evens out over time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the outgoing group say to the incoming group: give it up, and it will be given up (in return)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the arrangement. Every group is both incoming and outgoing at different times, so why not cancel the extra loaves and split everything evenly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every משמר is incoming one time and outgoing another time. Over time, then, each group gains the two loaves once and loses them once. The challenge is that the extra payment seems pointless, so the groups should be able to drop it and divide six and six.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him
Remove for remove: you give up yours and I give up mine (it evens out)

phrases.english: But let (the outgoing group) say to him: remove in exchange for remove!
phrases.notes: Meaning: let's cancel the extra on both sides, since it balances out anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical sense of the payment described in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The arrangement of giving the incoming group two extra loaves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each group is incoming and outgoing in turn, so the extra evens out and could simply be waived by both sides.

steps.title: A sure gain now is better
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a proverb: a ripe cucumber now is better than a big gourd later.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A good cucumber (now) is better than a gourd (later).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that people prefer a small, sure gain right now over a bigger gain they might get later. So the incoming group won't agree to give up the loaves it can take today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The math may balance out in theory, but the incoming group holds the loaves in hand right now. Its future turn is distant and uncertain. People do not trade a sure present benefit for a promised future one, so the arrangement stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Than a gourd (big but not yet ripe)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A good cucumber (now) is better than a gourd (later).
phrases.notes: A folk proverb: an immediate small gain beats a larger future gain.

steps.whatToRemember: The incoming משמר gets two extra loaves as wages for locking the doors. It won't trade that away, because a sure gain now is better than a possible gain later.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since it evens out, the groups would cancel the extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: People prefer an immediate gain, so the incoming group keeps the extra loaves.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the מוספין are also divided
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה adds that the two groups also divide (the hides of) the מוספין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: And they divide the מוספין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה makes a new statement. Besides the bread, the incoming and outgoing groups also share the מוספין (the שבת additional offerings), meaning their hides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentioned dividing the לחם הפנים. רב יהודה adds a second item that is shared between the groups on the changeover שבת. This statement becomes the target of the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional offerings brought on שבת and holidays

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
And they (also) divide the Musaf offerings.
phrases.notes: Meaning the hides of the מוספין, which go to the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement adding to the משנה's list of shared items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The incoming and outgoing משמרות share the מוספין (their hides).

steps.title: A ברייתא that leaves out dividing the מוספין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא that lists the duties of each group but says nothing about dividing the מוספין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: The outgoing משמר does the morning תמיד and the מוספין; the incoming משמר does the afternoon תמיד and the בזיכין (frankincense bowls). Yet it does not teach 'they divide the מוספין'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with a ברייתא. The ברייתא describes what each group does on the changeover שבת and never mentions dividing the מוספין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא, the outgoing group does the מוספין. That sounds like the outgoing group owns them, with no sharing. Its silence about dividing the מוספין seems to contradict רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected (a challenge from a תנאית source)
The bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The outgoing watch performs
the morning Tamid and the Musaf offerings,
the incoming watch performs
the afternoon Tamid and the frankincense bowls —
yet 'they divide the Musaf offerings' it does not teach!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's statement in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that the מוספין are divided.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא listing the changeover duties assigns the מוספין to the outgoing group and never mentions dividing them.

steps.title: That ברייתא isn't discussing division
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא is only discussing who does the service, not how the portions are divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא is not speaking about division.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה. The ברייתא's topic is who performs which service, so we should not expect it to mention sharing portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence only proves something if the source is dealing with that subject. This ברייתא covers the jobs, not the dividing up of portions, so its silence does not disprove רב יהודה.

phrases.english: This Tanna, about division
is not speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא בַּחֲלוּקָּה לָא קָא מַיְירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's silence means the מוספין are not divided.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only deals with the assignment of service, so its silence proves nothing.

steps.title: רבא: the School of שמואל discusses division and still omits it
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the ברייתא of דבי שמואל. It does discuss dividing the bread, yet it still says nothing about dividing the מוספין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But the תנא of דבי שמואל speaks about division, and it does not teach 'they divide the מוספין'! As דבי שמואל taught: The outgoing משמר does the morning תמיד and the מוספין; the incoming משמר does the afternoon תמיד and the בזיכין. Four כהנים would enter there, two from this משמר and two from that משמר, and they divide the לחם הפנים. Yet it does not teach 'they divide the מוספין'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא renews the challenge with a stronger source. This ברייתא explicitly talks about dividing the לחם הפנים, so the previous answer no longer works, and it still leaves out the מוספין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier defense was that the ברייתא wasn't discussing division. The ברייתא of דבי שמואל clearly is discussing division, since it describes four כהנים splitting the bread. If the מוספין were also divided, it should have said so, and its silence now strongly counts against רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study house of שמואל

phrases.english: Rava said:
But the Tanna of the School of Shmuel,
who does speak about division,
and still does not teach 'they divide the Musaf'?
As the School of Shmuel taught:
The outgoing watch performs
the morning Tamid and the Musaf offerings,
the incoming watch performs
the afternoon Tamid and the frankincense bowls.
Four priests would enter there (the Sanctuary).
phrases.notes: They entered to remove the old bread and set out the new bread.

phrases.english: two from this watch,
and two from that watch,
and they divide the showbread.
yet 'they divide the Musaf offerings' it does not teach!

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mistake this for a repeat of step 6. The first half of this ברייתא sounds the same, but this one goes on to talk about dividing the bread. That is exactly why the earlier answer ('it isn't discussing division') no longer works.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל דְּמַיְירִי בַּחֲלוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the answer of step 7 with a source that does discuss division.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim, and the defense in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא that explicitly discusses dividing portions mentions only the bread, implying the מוספין are not divided.

steps.title: רב יהודה is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב יהודה's statement is conclusively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב יהודה! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that רב יהודה's view has been disproven, and confirms it with no further answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No defense is offered against the ברייתא of דבי שמואל. The word תיובתא means the opinion is rejected. The halacha therefore does not follow רב יהודה's claim that the מוספין are divided.

phrases.english: A refutation of Rav Yehuda!
It is a refutation.

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה said the מוספין are also divided. The ברייתא of דבי שמואל discusses dividing portions and mentions only the bread, so רב יהודה is refuted.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 8 as decisive.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה's view that the מוספין are divided is rejected.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the incoming divide in the north
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which says the incoming group divides its bread in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The incoming divide in the north.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and quotes it. This is a setup step that prepares for the ברייתא explaining the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that the incoming group divides its share of the bread in the northern part of the עזרה. The reason is not given yet. The ברייתא in the next step supplies it.

phrases.english: The incoming divide (the bread) in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The incoming משמר divides its bread in the north of the עזרה.

steps.title: Why north for incoming and south for outgoing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the locations make it visible who is coming in and who is going out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The incoming divide in the north, so that it will be seen that they are coming in; and the outgoing divide in the south, so that it will be seen that they are going out.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the reason for the משנה's rule. Each group divides in a set place so that onlookers can clearly tell who is starting their shift and who is ending it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The north side of the עזרה is the more important area, where the holiest offerings are slaughtered. Putting the incoming group there marks it as the group now taking over. Putting the outgoing group in the south marks it as the group stepping down, so the changeover is visible to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it will be seen

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The incoming divide in the north —
so that it will be seen that they are coming in,
and the outgoing divide in the south —
so that it will be seen that they are going out.

steps.whatToRemember: The incoming group divides in the north and the outgoing group in the south, so that everyone can see who is coming in and who is leaving.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The division locations make it publicly visible which group is entering and which is leaving.

steps.title: בילגה always divides in the south
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the משמר of בילגה always divides its bread in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: בילגה always divides in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can explain it next. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the incoming משמר divides in the north, which is the more honored side. בילגה is an exception: even when coming in, it divides in the south. That looks like a penalty, and the גמרא will now explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: South, the side of the outgoing group

phrases.english: Bilga always divides in the south.
phrases.notes: Even when it is the incoming group, which should divide in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה after the explanation that the locations show who is coming in and who is going out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בילגה divides in the south even when it is the incoming group.

steps.title: The story of מרים בת בילגה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how מרים בת בילגה abandoned her faith, kicked the מזבח, and insulted it. In response, the חכמים disabled her משמר's ring and sealed its niche.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman from the בילגה family left her religion and married a Greek officer. When the Greeks entered the Temple, she kicked the מזבח and mocked it: 'Wolf! You eat up the Jews' money but do not help them when they are in trouble!' When the חכמים heard this, they penalized her whole משמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the first reason for בילגה's penalty: a shocking story about a member of their family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each משמר had its own ring in the עזרה for slaughtering animals and its own wall niche for storing knives. By fixing the ring in place and sealing the niche, the חכמים publicly shamed בילגה. Dividing in the south is part of the same penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: A ring in the עזרה used to hold animals for slaughter
A wall niche for storing knives

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמִרְיָם בַּת בִּילְגָּה
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: There was an incident with Miriam, daughter of Bilga,
who abandoned her religion,
and went and married a certain soldier
of the Greek kings.
When the Greeks entered the Sanctuary,

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה מְבַעֶטֶת בְּסַנְדָּלָהּ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: she was kicking with her sandal on top of the altar,
and said: Wolf, wolf!

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מְכַלֶּה מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: Until when will you consume the money of Israel

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה עוֹמֵד עֲלֵיהֶם בִּשְׁעַת הַדְּחָק!
phrases.english: and not stand up for them in their time of trouble!
When the Sages heard about the matter,
they fixed its ring in place
phrases.notes: So that בילגה could not use its own ring.

phrases.english: and sealed its niche.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמִרְיָם בַּת בִּילְגָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה's rule quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בילגה was penalized because of מרים's act against the מזבח.

steps.title: Another reason: בילגה's משמר came late
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says the penalty came because בילגה's משמר arrived late, so the משמר of their brother ישבב stayed and served in their place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: his משמר was late in coming, so ישבב his brother came in with him and served in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a different explanation for why בילגה was penalized: the group did not show up on time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the penalty is for the whole group's own failure, not one person's sin. ישבב was the משמר just before בילגה, so its members stayed and did בילגה's work.

phrases.english: And some say: his shift was late in coming,
and Yeshevav his brother entered with him
and served in his place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reason for the same penalty given in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בילגה was penalized because its משמר came late.

steps.title: בילגה's neighbors gained
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes an unusual result: usually neighbors of the wicked suffer, but here ישבב gained, because it always divides in the honored north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though neighbors of wicked people usually do not gain, בילגה's neighbors did gain. בילגה always divides in the south, and his brother ישבב always divides in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a side point about the outcome of the penalty: ישבב, the neighbor, benefited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the outgoing group divides in the south. Since בילגה is stuck in the south, ישבב, who goes out right when בילגה comes in, gets the north even though it is outgoing. This exception sets up the saying 'אוי לרשע אוי לשכינו' that appears at the end of the מסכת.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁכֵינֵי הָרְשָׁעִים לֹא נִשְׂתַּכְּרוּ,
phrases.english: Even though neighbors of the wicked do not profit,
Bilga's neighbors did profit,
since Bilga always divides in the south,
and Yeshevav his brother in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁכֵינֵי הָרְשָׁעִים לֹא נִשְׂתַּכְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a note about how the penalty affected the neighboring משמר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישבב always divides in the north because of בילגה's penalty.

steps.title: Why punish the father for his daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the מרים explanation. Lateness justifies punishing the whole משמר, but why should בילגה himself, the father, be penalized because of his daughter's sin?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the opinion that the משמר came late. That is why we penalize the whole group. But according to the opinion that it was because מרים בת בילגה left her religion, do we penalize him because of his daughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the fairness of the first explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the lateness explanation, the whole group did wrong, so a group penalty makes sense. Under the מרים explanation, only one woman sinned, so the גמרא asks why her father and the whole משמר should suffer.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (according to one view)

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ שׁוֹהָה לָבֹא,
phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says his shift was late in coming;
that is why we penalize the entire shift.
But according to the one who says
it was because Miriam, daughter of Bilga, abandoned her religion,
do we penalize him because of his daughter?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ שׁוֹהָה לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two reasons and challenges the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that בילגה was penalized because of מרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A father should not be penalized for his daughter's personal sin. Only under the lateness explanation did the group itself do wrong.

steps.title: A child repeats what is heard at home
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers yes: מרים must have heard such talk from her parents.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Yes. As people say: what a child says in the marketplace comes either from his father or from his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the penalty by blaming the home where מרים grew up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרים's insult was not her own invention; she learned that attitude from her parents. So the father shares the blame.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Yes,
as people say:
the speech of a child in the marketplace
is either his father's or his mother's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only מרים sinned, so her father is innocent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her words reflect her parents' talk, so they share responsibility.

steps.title: Why punish the whole shift for the parents?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: even if the parents are to blame, why penalize the entire משמר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of her father and mother, do we penalize the whole משמר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question on אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי explained why the parents are guilty. But the penalty fell on the whole group, which includes many families who did nothing wrong.

phrases.english: And because of her father and mother
do we penalize the entire shift?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם אֲבוּהּ וְאִימֵּיהּ קָנְסִינַן לְכוּלַּהּ מִשְׁמָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's answer that the parents share the blame.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Guilty parents still do not explain punishing all the other families in the משמר.

steps.title: Woe to the wicked, woe to his neighbor
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the wicked bring harm on those near them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Woe to the wicked one, and woe to his neighbor.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that being close to evil people brings harm on the people around them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the משמר was punished because it was connected to the wicked family. This is the general rule that step 15 called the normal pattern, and בילגה's case fits it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אוֹי לָרָשָׁע אוֹי לִשְׁכֵינוֹ,
phrases.english: Abaye said: Woe to the wicked, woe to his neighbor,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אוֹי לָרָשָׁע אוֹי לִשְׁכֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the guilty family should be penalized.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wicked bring harm on those connected to them, so the whole משמר suffers.

steps.title: Good for the righteous, good for his neighbor
steps.stepSummary: The מסכת ends on a positive note: the righteous bring good to their neighbors, supported by a verse in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Good for the righteous one, good for his neighbor, as it says: 'Say of the righteous that it is good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes מסכת סוכה by turning the harsh rule around into a blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the plural 'they will eat', even though it speaks about one צדיק. This shows that the people around the צדיק also enjoy his reward. So the מסכת ends with hope instead of punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (a verse follows)

steps.whatToRemember: בילגה was penalized either because of מרים's insult to the מזבח or because the משמר came late. The wicked harm their neighbors, but the righteous bring good to their neighbors.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a well-known custom to end a מסכת on a positive note. Here the closing teaches the value of living near righteous people and the danger of living near wicked ones.

phrases.english: Good for the righteous, good for his neighbor,
as it is said: 'Say of the righteous that it is good,
for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 3:10. 'They' in the plural hints that the neighbors share the reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive counterpart of אביי's rule in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Just as the wicked harm their neighbors, the righteous benefit their neighbors.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק החליל and מסכת סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The formal closing line: we have finished פרק החליל, and with it all of מסכת סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'The Flute' chapter, and with this מסכת סוכה is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the last פרק, החליל, and the end of the whole מסכת סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הדרן means 'we will return,' a promise to come back and learn this פרק again. The added phrase וסליקא לה מסכת סוכה tells us this was the last פרק, so the whole מסכת is done. It follows right after the hopeful closing teaching that the righteous bring good to those near them.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The closing words said when finishing a פרק.
'The flute.' The name of the fifth and last פרק of מסכת סוכה, taken from its opening words.
And it is finished. Used when the whole מסכת is complete.
The tractate dealing with the laws of סוכה, לולב, and the celebrations of סוכות.

steps.whatToRemember: The הדרן is a closing formula, not part of the debate. It shows love for the learning and a promise to come back to it. Finishing a whole מסכת is a time for a סיום.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read הדרן as another step in the argument about משמרת בלגה. That discussion ended in the previous step. This line only marks the end of the פרק and the מסכת.
steps.whyThisMatters: Completing a מסכת is traditionally celebrated with a סיום, and the הדרן text is recited at that time. This shows that Torah learning is meant to be reviewed again and again.

phrases.english: We will return to you, [the chapter] 'The Flute'
phrases.notes: The standard closing formula for a פרק.

phrases.english: and Tractate Sukkah is completed
phrases.notes: Added because this is the final פרק of the מסכת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comes after the closing teaching in step 20 and formally ends the פרק and the מסכת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק החליל and all of מסכת סוכה are complete. We commit to return and learn them again.
